## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Honor `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` so CI can configure exclusions without passing command-line arguments.

## Changes

The pull request adds and documents a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that filters files by basename and logs skipped paths in verbose mode. It adds tests for parsing, filtering, and archive contents.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` argument, the archive still includes `build.log` because the parser hardcodes `default=[]`. `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires that “Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable”. — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment will produce archives containing the files they configured the tool to skip.

## Suggestions

- tests/test_main.py:20 — tests — Verify repeated exclusions in the archive — With `--exclude '*.log' --exclude '*.tmp'`, the repeatability test passes if the archive uses only the first pattern and includes `cache.tmp`. It checks the parser’s list, and the archive test supplies a single pattern. — A regression that drops later exclusions during archive creation would pass the current suite. — Fix: Extend `test_main_leaves_excluded_files_out_of_the_archive` to exercise repeated flags.
